messages.subject: Non-deterministic behaviour of INLA
parts:
Hi all, 
I'm tring to get INLA to model the effects of some covariates on a y variable and have encountered a strange problem. Everytime I run INLA it comes up with a different result.  We've found that the logs change when optimiszing theta within a couple of lines. Is this a bug or something to do with my variables/ partciualr model? We've checked seeds, environment changes and clean terminals. First runs on clean terminals are also different. I've attached my code and raster variables. The script runs the model 20 times in two selfcontained environments. This script does stabalise it a bit but it's still changing between runs. Any help would be greatly appreciated. 
Best wishes, 
Kian

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: Non-deterministic behaviour of INLA
parts:
You will get minor differences due to the parallelisation done, where the number
of threads used, and how they are used, make a small difference. this is
controlled by the run-time system outside of our control.

if you want exactly the same results, you can get that with

inla.setOption(num.threads = 1, internal.opt = FALSE)

(where internal.opt might chose different algorithms for doing stuff based on
timing, which may results in different algs doing the same thing, which will
give epsilon different results)

the attached is what you get with the options above

messages.author: 9a89594e7fcb7aad
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: Non-deterministic behaviour of INLA
parts:
then I think you run an old version of INLA (and I guess also an old version of
R)

if so, please upgrade R to 4.4 and to the most recent testing version

since in general,

(a + b) + c != a + (b + c)

with finite numerics, then parallem computations will in general give slightly
different results.

if you want to avoid it, you can set num.threads=1
